newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Enron wins Brazil power plant bid.
newsitem.headline: Enron wins Brazil power plant bid.

text.p: A Brazilian subsidiary of U.S. energy giant Enron Corp. has won a bid to build, operate and own a 480-megawatt thermoelectric power station in Mato Grosso state, western Brazil, officials said Friday.
Empresa Produtora de Energia Ltda., which is 100 percent owned by Enron, was awarded the contract by Eletronorte, part of the federal Eletrobras holding, Thursday.

"We're very happy to have been chosen to meet the region's energy needs and to bring the benefits of natural gas to Mato Grosso, one of fastest growing areas of the country," said Enron do Brasil president James Bannantine in a statement.
No details of the value of the project were released but news reports put the cost at about $500 million.

During a initial first-year phase, the power project will run on diesel fuel to produce up to 150 megawatts. By the second year, the plant would using natural gas to generate 300 megawatts, rising to 480 megawatts by the end of the third year.
The natural gas would come from a new pipeline to be built linking the gasfields of Bolivia with Brazil's industrial southeast and other regions.
Enron is one of several international power companies involved in the upcoming construction and future operation of the $2.0 billion pipeline.
Brazil is seeking to encourage private companies to build new power stations and complete unfinished projects to bolster its cash-strapped, publicly-owned electricity industry.
Two federally owned power distributors have already been sold and privatization of Eletrobras' four generating companies is expected to begin next year.
